title: Meaningful Commit Messages
overview: Commit messages should clearly describe what changes were made so the project history remains understandable.

example.title: Commit Example
example.content:
Good:
Add user authentication flow

Bad:
Changes done

title: Keep Commits Small
overview: Small commits are easier to review, debug, and understand compared to large unrelated changes.

example.title: Better Practice
example.content:
Separate commits:

1. Add UI
2. Add Validation
3. Connect API

title: Branch Management
overview: Using proper branch naming and removing unused branches keeps repositories organized.

title: Avoid Committing Sensitive Data
overview: Sensitive information like passwords, API keys, and environment files should never be committed.

title: Regular Pull and Updates
overview: Keeping the local repository updated helps avoid conflicts and keeps developers synchronized.

example.title: Update Flow
example.content:
git pull
 ↓
Make Changes
 ↓
Commit
 ↓
Push

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned Git practices for better commits, branches, security, collaboration, and repository management.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:
✔ Write clear commits.
✔ Protect sensitive data.
✔ Keep branches clean.
✔ Sync regularly.
